title: Normal base branch conjugacy
statement: Let $A\to B$ be an injective local map of complete DVRs with fraction fields $K\subseteq L$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring, def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring, def-pc-field-extension]. Let $K_1/K$ be finite normal, not necessarily separable, where normal means splitting of irreducible polynomials having a root. Let $A_1$ be the integral closure of $A$ in $K_1$ and $B_1$ the integral closure of $B$ in $(L\otimes_KK_1)_{\mathrm{red}}$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. The group $\operatorname{Aut}_K(K_1)$ acts on $A_1$ and $B_1$ and transitively on the maximal ideals of $B_1$. It preserves the unique maximal ideal of $A_1$. Consequently the ramification indices of $A_1\to (B_1)_q$ are independent of $q$; if one equals $1$ then all equal $1$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Here the ramification index $e$ is determined by $\mathfrak m_{A_1}(B_1)_q=(q(B_1)_q)^e$, and reduction means quotient by nilpotents.

source.place: Tag 09EU, lemma-galois-relative, and its transitive action on the normalized maximal ideals; completeness makes the lower normalization local.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-dvr-algebraic-normalization-structure], case (a), with $P=K_1$: $R=(L\otimes_KK_1)_{\mathrm{red}}$ is a nonempty finite product $\prod_{i\in I}L_i$ of fields. Each $L_i/L$ is finite: a finite $K$-basis of $K_1$ spans the tensor, hence every factor, over $L$. Let $C_i$ be the integral closure of $B$ in $L_i$. Let $D\in\{A,B\}$, $F$ the finite extension $K_1$ resp. $L_i$ of its fraction field, $N\in\{A_1,C_i\}$ its integral closure in $F$. As $D$ is a principal ideal domain it is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-pid-noetherian-normal], so [lem-weil-pbc-complete-local-nagata] makes $D=D/(0)$ N-2 [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring, def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain]: $N$ is a finite $D$-module. Being a domain, $N$ is local and complete, and its maximal ideal is the only prime of $N$ over $\mathfrak m_D$, by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-complete-local-product]. $D$ has Krull dimension one [lem-sc-dvr-dimension-one], so [lem-sfb-finite-normalization-local-dvr] gives a prime $\mathfrak q\subset N$ over $\mathfrak m_D$ with $N_{\mathfrak q}$ a DVR of fraction field $F$ and $\mathfrak m_{N_{\mathfrak q}}\cap D=\mathfrak m_D$; $\mathfrak q$ is the maximal ideal of local $N$, so $N=N_{\mathfrak q}$. Hence $A_1$ and every $C_i$ are complete DVRs, local over $A$ and $B$. Moreover $B_1=\prod_i C_i$: projection preserves a monic equation; conversely, if each coordinate satisfies a monic polynomial $f_i$ over $B$, the monic product $\prod_i f_i$ annihilates the tuple. The maximal ideals of this finite product are precisely $q_i=C_1\times\cdots\times\mathfrak m_{C_i}\times\cdots$; their localizations are $C_i$. Indeed a prime contains all but one of the orthogonal coordinate idempotents, and then is the inverse image of a prime of that coordinate. This identifies maximal ideals with $I$. The same structure node says each $q_i$ contracts to a maximal ideal of $A_1$; since $A_1$ is local this is its unique maximal ideal, so all $A_1\to C_i$ are local DVR maps.

source.place: Tag 09EM, remark-construction (1), (3), (4), (5); finite complete normalization also in Tag 09F8, lemma-special-case, first proof paragraph.

proof.text: For $\sigma\in G=\operatorname{Aut}_K(K_1)$ define $1\otimes\sigma$ on the tensor algebra. The tensor universal property [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] gives its inverse $1\otimes\sigma^{-1}$ and the group law. An automorphism preserves nilpotents, so this descends to $R$. Applying $\sigma$ to a monic equation over $A$ preserves its coefficients, and applying $1\otimes\sigma$ to a monic equation over $B$ does likewise. Thus [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] restricts these actions to $A_1$ and $B_1$. Their square commutes because it does on $K_1\to R$, $a\mapsto\overline{1\otimes a}$. The action on $A_1$ fixes its unique maximal ideal: an automorphism carries a maximal ideal to a maximal ideal.

source.place: Tag 09EU, lemma-galois-relative, first assertion: restriction of the tensor action to integral elements.

proof.text: A ring automorphism of $R=\prod_{i\in I}L_i$ permutes the primitive coordinate idempotents: an idempotent has only $0$ or $1$ in each field coordinate, and the nonzero ones which cannot be expressed as a sum of two nonzero orthogonal idempotents are exactly the single-coordinate ones. Suppose this permutation action has more than one orbit. Choose one orbit $J\subsetneq I$ and let $b\in R$ have coordinate $1$ on $J$ and $0$ elsewhere. Then $b$ is fixed by every element of $G$, $b^2=b$, and $b\ne0,1$. By [lem-sfb-normal-tensor-invariant-powers], $b^N=\overline{l\otimes1}$ for some $N\geq1$ and $l\in L$. Since $b^N=b$, the scalar $l$ is idempotent. The scalar map $L\to R$ is injective: it is a unital map from a field to the nonzero ring $R$ of step 1. Thus $l^2=l$ implies $l=0$ or $1$, a contradiction. The action is therefore transitive on $I$. The product $B_1=\prod_i C_i$ has the same coordinate idempotents as $R$; the actions agree by restriction, and each $C_i$ has exactly one maximal ideal. Hence the induced action is transitive on the maximal ideals $q_i$ of $B_1$.

source.place: Tag 09EU, lemma-galois-relative, invariant-element contradiction; orbit idempotents replace the Chinese-remainder norm, with the inseparable fixed-field correction in the new input.

proof.text: Given maximal ideals $q,q^{\prime}$ of $B_1$, choose $\sigma\in G$ sending $q$ to $q^{\prime}$. Its localization is the isomorphism $\phi:(B_1)_q\to(B_1)_{q^{\prime}}$, $b/s\mapsto\sigma(b)/\sigma(s)$; the denominator avoids $q^{\prime}$ exactly when $s$ avoids $q$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. It restricts to the automorphism $\sigma$ of $A_1$, and so sends $\mathfrak m_{A_1}(B_1)_q$ onto $\mathfrak m_{A_1}(B_1)_{q^{\prime}}$, and $q(B_1)_q$ onto $q^{\prime}(B_1)_{q^{\prime}}$. To see that the indices exist, choose uniformizers $a$ in $A_1$ and $t$ in $(B_1)_q$. The image of $a$ is nonzero and is a nonunit because the map is injective and local (step 1). By [lem-weil-pbc-dvr-unit-times-uniformizer-power] it is $ut^e$ for a unit $u$ and an integer $e\geq1$. This gives $\mathfrak m_{A_1}(B_1)_q=(t)^e$. The exponent is unique: if $(t)^e=(t)^f$ with $e<f$, then $t^e=ct^f$ for some $c$, cancellation in the domain makes $t$ a unit, a contradiction. Transport the ideal equality along $\phi$ to obtain the same exponent at $q^{\prime}$. Thus every branch has the same ramification index, and an index of $1$ at one branch forces index $1$ everywhere.

source.place: Tag 09F8, lemma-special-case, proof: all branch extensions are isomorphic; ramification is defined by powers of maximal ideals. Uniformizer factorization: Tag 00PD, algebra-lemma-characterize-dvr.

The DVR is Noetherian because it is a PID (lem-weil-pbc-pid-noetherian-normal). It is Nagata by lem-weil-pbc-complete-local-nagata (Algebra 032W), so it is N-2 and N is finite over it. N is a finite domain, so it is local and complete with a unique prime over m by lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-complete-local-product (Algebra 0325). The base has dimension 1 (lem-sc-dvr-dimension-one), and lem-sfb-finite-normalization-local-dvr gives N_q a DVR; since N is local, N_q = N. I checked every hypothesis: the extensions K_1/K and L_i/L are finite, and no separability is needed. proof_deps is rebuilt as the union of the uses, and split_report.tool_uses is replaced by the two sk-thm-p1 Algebra tools. The fixed closure has 231 nodes, contains no dropped id and has no cycle. Steps 2-4 are unchanged and correct: the tensor universal property gives the actions; transitivity follows from a fixed orbit idempotent, the new node and injectivity of L into R; ramification indices are equal because the localization isomorphism carries one to the other, using the unit-times-uniformizer-power node. The new node lem-sfb-normal-tensor-invariant-powers is true: lift x, take a common p-power so the lift is invariant, invariants of the tensor are L tensor E^G, E^G/K is purely inseparable (Fields 030M), and in characteristic 0 one can take N=1. I tested it with E=K, with E/K purely inseparable, with C tensor_R C, and with L/K infinite. It is statement-only, strictly smaller than the item, and has no duplicate in the DAG. The source error is genuine: the 09EU proof uses K=(K_1)^G, which fails for an inseparable normal extension, for example F_p(t^{1/p})/F_p(t). The item statement is unchanged.
